llm_analysis.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
llm_analysis.takeaway: FLORE addresses force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation, where contact force must be coordinated across both hands and the whole body rather than specified by kinematics alone. It collects robot-free demonstrations with two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers and wearable body trackers, then trains a force-reactive diffusion policy on vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches to predict actions and per-hand force commands, executed by a hybrid compliance whole-body controller whose integral force-error term uses real F/T sensors for directional force tracking and off-direction compliance. Reported evidence includes simulation tracking of varied per-hand force commands with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy, and 80% success versus 26.7% for a position-only policy on three contact-rich robot tasks. Inspect how force commands are represented and how the controller balances force tracking against balance.

llm_analysis.title: Robot-Aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Precise Reaching with Wrist-Camera VLA Policies
llm_analysis.takeaway: This benchmark-style work targets data collection for wrist-camera VLA policies in precise pre-contact reaching, motivated by electronic-waste disassembly where densely packed, visually similar parts make full digital-twin simulation difficult. It reconstructs the real workspace with 3D Gaussian Splatting, renders diverse wrist-camera observations from robot-aligned poses, and pairs them with smooth structured reaching trajectories for VLA fine-tuning, adding an instruction-conditioned reach verifier that estimates target proximity and terminates before physical interaction. In motherboard disassembly experiments with π0.5, 1,500 generated trajectories reach 80.0% precise-reaching success across three targets versus 58.7% from 150 teleoperated demonstrations, using under 10 minutes of active human capture. Inspect how robot-aligned rendering and the verifier affect evaluation validity.

llm_analysis.title: Touch Begins Where Vision Ends: Generalizable Policies for Contact-Rich Manipulation
llm_analysis.takeaway: ViTaL tackles fine-grained contact-rich manipulation by decomposing tasks into a reaching phase, where a vision-language model performs scene-level reasoning to localize the object, and a local interaction phase, where a reusable scene-agnostic policy uses egocentric vision and tactile sensing. The premise is that scene context varies while low-level interaction stays consistent, so local policies trained once in a canonical setting can generalize through localize-then-execute. The abstract reports around 90% success on contact-rich tasks in unseen environments and robustness to distractors, with ablations supporting segmentation-based visual encoder training via behavior cloning, improved generalizability of residual-RL policies, and tactile sensing gains. Inspect the canonical-setting training setup and the ablation design.

llm_analysis.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
llm_analysis.takeaway: TrySee examines closed-loop robot task planning with general-purpose VLMs in specialized domains where image interpretation and grounding are weak. It is a modular pipeline combining reactive cyclic planning with domain-specific modular vision preprocessing for online grounding, plus a dynamic preprocessing selection mechanism for scalability, and it requires neither VLM fine-tuning nor end-to-end demonstrations, adapting through replaceable perception modules and motion planning. Evaluation spans planning tasks in 5 widely different domains, including a real-world robot disassembly task, and field tests in a brownfield environment are reported to demonstrate practicality when domain-specific training data are limited. Inspect how preprocessing selection is triggered and how grounding failures propagate through the loop.

paper.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
paper.summary: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.

paper.title: Robot-Aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Precise Reaching with Wrist-Camera VLA Policies
paper.summary: Efficient robotic data collection remains a major bottleneck for vision-language-action (VLA) policy learning, especially for tasks requiring accurate end-effector positioning and camera-action alignment. This challenge is particularly severe in electronic-waste disassembly, where robots operate in cluttered assemblies of densely packed, visually similar components. Full digital-twin simulation is difficult because many parts are thin, reflective, or mechanically complex, making accurate object-level meshes and contact models difficult to obtain. In this work, we focus on pre-contact reaching and propose a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based data generation pipeline for wrist-camera VLA adaptation. Our method reconstructs the real workspace with 3DGS and renders diverse wrist-camera observations from robot-aligned poses. These observations are paired with smooth, structured reaching trajectories to provide robot-aligned visual-action supervision for VLA fine-tuning. We further augment the VLA policy with an instruction-conditioned reach verifier that estimates target proximity and provides reliable termination before physical interaction. Experiments in motherboard disassembly demonstrate precise VLA-based reaching using wrist-camera observations alone, without an external side-view camera. With $π$0.5, 1,500 generated trajectories achieve 80.0\% precise-reaching success across three targets, compared with 58.7\% using 150 teleoperated demonstrations, while requiring less than 10 minutes of active human capture. Project website: https://001-wang.github.io/PrecisionReach-GS/

historical_paper.title: Touch Begins Where Vision Ends: Generalizable Policies for Contact-Rich Manipulation
historical_paper.abstract: Data-driven approaches struggle with precise manipulation; imitation learning requires many hard-to-obtain demonstrations, while reinforcement learning yields brittle, non-generalizable policies. We introduce VisuoTactile Local (ViTaL) policy learning, a framework that solves fine-grained manipulation tasks by decomposing them into two phases: a reaching phase, where a vision-language model (VLM) enables scene-level reasoning to localize the object of interest, and a local interaction phase, where a reusable, scene-agnostic ViTaL policy performs contact-rich manipulation using egocentric vision and tactile sensing. This approach is motivated by the observation that while scene context varies, the low-level interaction remains consistent across task instances. By training local policies once in a canonical setting, they can generalize via a localize-then-execute strategy. ViTaL achieves around 90% success on contact-rich tasks in unseen environments and is robust to distractors. ViTaL's effectiveness stems from three key insights: (1) foundation models for segmentation enable training robust visual encoders via behavior cloning; (2) these encoders improve the generalizability of policies learned using residual RL; and (3) tactile sensing significantly boosts performance in contact-rich tasks. Ablation studies validate each of these insights, and we demonstrate that ViTaL integrates well with high-level VLMs, enabling robust, reusable low-level skills. Results and videos are available at https://vitalprecise.github.io.

paper.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
paper.summary: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in high-level reasoning and task planning for robots. However, specialized domains remain a challenge for VLMs' image interpretation and grounding abilities. We introduce TrySee, a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline integrating general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception and established robotics components. The system consists of an inherently reactive cyclic planning pipeline, augmented with domain-specific modular vision preprocessing, to provide online grounding. Finally, a dynamic preprocessing selection mechanism contributes to the scalability of the pipeline. The system requires neither VLM fine-tuning nor end-to-end demonstrations and adapts through replaceable perception modules and motion planning. The approach is evaluated on planning tasks across 5 widely different domains, including a real-world robot disassembly task. The field tests in a brownfield environment demonstrate the approach's practicality in integrating VLM planning into specialized robotic systems with limited domain-specific training data.
